overview: Deere & Company (John Deere) is the global leader in agricultural, construction, forestry, and turf equipment, manufacturing products ranging from large row-crop tractors and combines to excavators, dozers, and roadbuilding machinery under the John Deere and Wirtgen brands. It operates through three equipment segments -- Production & Precision Agriculture (PPA), Small Agriculture & Turf (SAT), and Construction & Forestry (CF) -- plus a captive Financial Services segment that finances dealer and customer purchases. Deere sells primarily through an independent dealer network (~2,050 US/Canada locations, distributors in 100+ countries) and is increasingly positioning itself as a technology company via its Smart Industrial Operating Model, precision-ag tools, and the John Deere Operations Center data platform.

business_model.summary: Deere earns the large majority of revenue from manufacturing and selling new and used heavy equipment (transactional, highly cyclical), supplemented by a high-margin, more durable aftermarket parts/service business and a captive finance arm (retail notes, leases, wholesale financing) that both earns net interest income and supports equipment sales. Precision-ag technology and nascent Solutions-as-a-Service (SaaS) subscriptions are a small but strategically important and growing recurring-revenue layer.

revenue_streams.name: Production & Precision Agriculture (large tractors, combines, cotton/sugarcane equipment)
revenue_streams.trend: declining (down 17% in FY2025; guided down ~10% in FY2026)
revenue_streams.basis: % of FY2025 equipment operations net sales

revenue_streams.name: Construction & Forestry (excavators, dozers, Wirtgen roadbuilding)
revenue_streams.trend: growing (FY2026 sales up double digits YoY through Q3)
revenue_streams.basis: % of FY2025 equipment operations net sales

revenue_streams.name: Small Agriculture & Turf (compact tractors, mowers, hay/forage)
revenue_streams.trend: growing (FY2026 sales up double digits YoY through Q3)
revenue_streams.basis: % of FY2025 equipment operations net sales

revenue_streams.name: Financial Services (retail notes, leases, wholesale financing, extended warranties)
revenue_streams.basis: reported separately; FY2025 segment revenue ~$6.3B including intercompany

business_model.customer_type: Predominantly B2B/B2C hybrid -- large-scale commercial row-crop farmers (PPA), small/dairy/turf and residential customers including mass retail via Home Depot/Lowe's (SAT), and construction/forestry/roadbuilding contractors (CF); sold through ~2,050 independent dealer locations in the US/Canada and distributors in 100+ other countries.
business_model.geographic_mix: U.S. and Canada are the majority of sales; nearly 80% of U.S.-sold product is assembled domestically. Meaningful exposure to Brazil/South America (ag), Europe (SAT, Wirtgen/CF), and growing presence in India and Asia; Deere is a net exporter of ag/turf equipment from the U.S.

competitive_position.market_position: Clear #1 in large North American row-crop agricultural equipment (4WD tractors, combines) with strong brand loyalty; a top-tier but not dominant player in construction equipment where Caterpillar and Komatsu are larger, and in compact/turf equipment where Kubota and Toro are strong regional competitors.

moat_factors.description: Dense, long-tenured independent dealer network (~2,050 US/Canada locations) provides sales, service, and financing support that is difficult for new entrants to replicate.
John Deere brand recognition commands premium pricing and resale value in North America, historically supporting a resilient used-equipment market.

John Deere Operations Center, AutoTrac guidance, and See & Spray create connectivity and switching-cost advantages, though customer adoption/monetization of SaaS offerings has been slower than management targets.
In-house financing (retail notes, leases, wholesale financing) smooths dealer and customer purchases and is a source of recurring, relatively stable earnings, but also adds credit and leverage risk.
Large global manufacturing footprint (23 owned/leased US/Canada factories, 45+ outside) and proprietary parts supply support cost position and aftermarket margins.

weaknesses: Heavy dependence on the cyclical North American large-ag market, which has been in a multi-year downturn (PPA net sales down 17% in FY2025)
Exposure to an antitrust/right-to-repair consent decree (settled July 2026) that constrains the historically profitable dealer-controlled service/parts model for up to 10 years
Slower-than-expected adoption and monetization of precision-ag and SaaS technology relative to Leap Ambitions targets
Significant tariff/trade-policy exposure as a large net exporter of U.S.-built agricultural equipment

growth_drivers: Precision agriculture technology adoption (AutoTrac guidance, See & Spray targeted spraying, S7 Series combines) driving productivity value and potential premium pricing/aftermarket pull-through
Expansion of Solutions-as-a-Service (SaaS) subscriptions and the John Deere Operations Center as a recurring-revenue layer, and continued investment in autonomy and AI-enabled equipment

Construction & Forestry growth tailwinds from U.S. infrastructure spending, data-center construction, and rental-fleet investment (Tenna LLC acquisition, Feb 2026, adds fleet/asset-tracking technology to CF)

Normalization of elevated used-equipment inventories (high-horsepower used tractor stock down ~40% YoY as of mid-2026), which management believes supports a new-equipment demand recovery as the ag cycle bottoms
Geographic expansion in Brazil (25th anniversary of operations in 2025, new Indaiatuba R&D center) and other emerging ag markets
Financial Services margin recovery as interest rates decline, improving financing spreads

business.description: Deere's results are tightly linked to farm income, commodity prices, and farmer sentiment; FY2025 net income fell ~29% and PPA operating profit fell 41% on declining market conditions.
Elevated used-inventory levels have depressed new-equipment price realization and volumes; although improving in 2026, a renewed buildup would again pressure sales.
Deere relies on independent dealers to manage inventory, financing, and customer relationships; dealer distress or inventory mismanagement can directly hurt Deere's sales and receivables.
Management has explicitly flagged slower-than-expected customer adoption of precision-ag and SaaS subscription offerings, delaying Leap Ambitions financial benefits.

financial.description: Allowance for credit losses on retail notes/leases rose in FY2025 on elevated ag/turf delinquencies; further farm-income deterioration could increase write-offs.
Financial Services interest-bearing debt-to-equity ratio was 8.6-to-1 at Q3 FY2026, typical for a captive finance arm but a source of refinancing and rate risk.
Material Brazilian real, Euro, and other foreign-currency exposure affects reported sales and financing results.

regulatory.description: July 2026 FTC/state settlement requires Deere to provide farmers and independent repair shops repair resources on par with authorized dealers for up to 10 years, under ongoing FTC oversight; a $99M consumer class-action settlement was also reached in April 2026.

Deere is a major net exporter of U.S.-built ag/turf equipment; incremental tariffs cost ~$600M in FY2025 and a net ~$502M in the first nine months of FY2026 even after a Feb 2026 Supreme Court ruling invalidating IEEPA tariffs produced ~$382M of recoveries.
Off-road engine emissions standards (U.S., EU, India) and climate-disclosure rules (EU CSRD, California SB-253/261) raise compliance and product-development costs.

macro.risk: Farm income and commodity price cycle
macro.description: Low commodity prices, high input costs, and farmer liquidity pressure are the primary drivers of the current ag-equipment downturn.
High rates raise dealer carrying costs and customer financing costs, dampening equipment demand, while also affecting Financial Services' financing spreads.
CF and turf segments are sensitive to residential/commercial construction activity, infrastructure spending, and interest-rate-driven investment decisions.
Tariffs, export controls, and conflicts (Russia/Ukraine, Middle East) affect input costs, supply chains, and commodity flows relevant to farm income.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Management describes FY2026 as the likely bottom of the current agricultural equipment cycle: large-ag (PPA) sales are guided down roughly 10% in FY2026 on top of a 17% FY2025 decline, while Small Ag & Turf and Construction & Forestry are both expected to grow, aided by infrastructure, data-center, and rental-fleet demand.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High -- agricultural equipment demand is historically cyclical, driven by farm income, commodity prices, and credit conditions; construction equipment is moderately cyclical, tied to housing and infrastructure spending.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate-to-high -- affects customer and dealer financing costs (demand channel) and Financial Services' financing spreads and funding costs (earnings channel); declining U.S. rates in 2025-2026 have been a modest tailwind.
key_input_costs: Tariff-affected imported components from Europe, Mexico, India, and Japan

recent_developments.event: FTC and five state attorneys general sued Deere alleging monopolization of agricultural equipment repair services (right-to-repair antitrust case).
Completed sale of 50% of Banco John Deere S.A. (Brazil financial services JV) to Banco Bradesco, deconsolidating BJD.

Reported FY2025 results: net income attributable to Deere fell to $5.03B from $7.10B in FY2024, driven by lower sales volumes, tariffs, and elevated used-equipment inventory; issued initial FY2026 net income guidance of $4.0-4.75B, below Street expectations at the time.
Acquired Tenna LLC, a U.S. construction fleet/asset-tracking technology company, for $439M, assigned to the Construction & Forestry segment.

U.S. Supreme Court invalidated tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (IEEPA); Deere recorded ~$382M of tariff recoveries in the first nine months of FY2026 (~80% received by Q3).
Reached a $99 million class-action settlement with equipment owners over right-to-repair restrictions.

Settled the FTC/state antitrust lawsuit via a consent decree requiring Deere to provide farmers and independent repair shops repair resources comparable to authorized dealers for up to 10 years, plus $1M to the plaintiff states.

Reported Q3 FY2026 results: net sales and revenues up 5% to $12.6B and net income up 7% to $1.38B; raised FY2026 net income guidance to $4.75-5.00B and said used high-horsepower tractor inventory was down ~40% YoY, reinforcing management's view that 2026 marks the bottom of the ag cycle.

items.metric: Net income attributable to Deere & Company
items.notes: Low end raised from $4.5B (original FY2026 guidance issued Nov 2025 was $4.0-4.75B); reflects stronger-than-expected CF and SAT performance offsetting weaker PPA.
Lifted alongside the net income guidance raise at Q3 FY2026.
Benefiting from favorable financing spreads and lower provision for credit losses, partially offset by a smaller average portfolio.
Revised to reflect softer conditions in South America and Europe; operating margin guided to 11-12%.

items.metric: Small Agriculture & Turf and Construction & Forestry net sales
items.notes: Both segments posted double-digit sales and operating-profit growth through the first nine months of FY2026.
Compares with $852M spent in the first nine months of FY2025 (through Q3 FY2026, $716M spent).

guidance.management_commentary: CEO John May reiterated that management continues to believe 2026 will mark the bottom of the current agricultural equipment cycle, citing improving early order program trends, declining used-equipment inventories, and increasing customer adoption of Deere's advanced technologies as reasons for confidence in long-term value creation.

bull_case: The agricultural equipment cycle appears to be bottoming in FY2026, with high-horsepower used-tractor inventory down ~40% YoY, setting up a potential new-equipment demand recovery into FY2027 and beyond

Construction & Forestry and Small Agriculture & Turf are both growing strongly (sales up double digits YoY through Q3 FY2026), diversifying Deere away from large-ag cyclicality and benefiting from infrastructure and data-center construction spending

Precision-ag technology (AutoTrac, See & Spray, S7 combines) and the John Deere Operations Center support a longer-term shift toward higher-margin, stickier technology and SaaS revenue that could structurally improve margins across cycles

Major legal overhangs have been resolved or reduced: the FTC right-to-repair lawsuit was settled in July 2026 and the related class action settled for $99M in April 2026, while the Supreme Court's IEEPA ruling is recovering a meaningful share of prior tariff costs

A captive, profitable Financial Services arm smooths equipment sales through the cycle and should benefit from improving financing spreads as interest rates decline, while Deere continues returning capital via buybacks and dividends
bear_case: Large agriculture (Production & Precision Ag) remains structurally weak -- down 17% in FY2025 and guided down a further ~10% in FY2026 -- on depressed farm income, high input costs, and global trade uncertainty, with no clear catalyst for a sharp recovery

Despite the IEEPA ruling, tariffs remain a material net cost (~$502M in the first nine months of FY2026), and U.S. trade policy remains unpredictable for a company that is a large net exporter of U.S.-built equipment

The 10-year FTC consent decree imposes ongoing compliance costs and oversight, and could over time erode the profitable dealer-controlled parts/service aftermarket that has long been a key competitive advantage

Monetization of precision-ag and SaaS technology investments has repeatedly lagged management's own Leap Ambitions targets, creating execution risk around a key part of the long-term growth and margin thesis

Elevated receivable write-offs and delinquencies in ag/turf retail financing could worsen if farm economics stay depressed for longer than expected, pressuring the highly levered Financial Services segment (8.6-to-1 debt-to-equity)
